# pushward_org_domain (Resource)

An email domain the organization claims, for single sign-on. Enterprise plan only.

It starts `pending`. Publish a TXT record named `txt_name` with the value `txt_value`, then verify it with `pushward_org_domain_verification`. A domain is verified by one organization at most, the first to verify it. PushWard looks the record up again every day and sets the domain back to `pending` after seven missed checks in a row, so keep the record; `status` then shows it, and replacing the verification (`terraform apply -replace`) verifies the domain again. Destroying it removes the domain; while single sign-on is on, PushWard refuses that for the organization's last verified domain.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Starts pending; publish the TXT record below, then verify it with
# pushward_org_domain_verification.
resource "pushward_org_domain" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

output "verification_record" {
  value = "${pushward_org_domain.example.txt_name} TXT \"${pushward_org_domain.example.txt_value}\""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) The domain, such as `example.com`. Not an IP address and not a public suffix such as `com` or `co.uk`. PushWard stores it lowercase, without a trailing dot, an internationalized domain in punycode (`xn--...`); the state keeps it as written here. Changing it to another domain replaces the domain; another spelling of the same one changes nothing in PushWard.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `org_id` (String) The organization the resource belongs to, that of the provider's org admin key when the resource was created or imported. An org admin key of another organization is an error, not a plan that creates the resource again there.
- `status` (String) `pending` or `verified`.
- `txt_name` (String) The DNS name of the TXT record that verifies the domain.
- `txt_value` (String) The TXT record's value.
- `verified_at` (String) When it was verified, RFC 3339; null while pending.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the domain, or by its id.
terraform import pushward_org_domain.example example.com
terraform import pushward_org_domain.example 6b1f0c2e-4d3a-4e5b-9c7d-8a0f1e2d3c4b
```
